clue.text: Rupert seen to be holding the castle

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: the castle in chess is also called a rook

explanation.surface: Someone called Rupert has been spotted occupying a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Brooke was the English poet of 'The Soldier', killed in the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet Rupert Brooke is the best-known bearer of the first name, so the surname is clued by it.

clue.text: Friar finally changes sides and turns into a low dive

indicators.note: the closing letter, R for right, is swapped for its opposite side, L for left

blocks.note: a friar is a brother in a religious order

explanation.surface: A friar abandons his order and ends up in a seedy drinking den.
explanation.walkthrough: BROTHER ends in R (right); changing sides turns it to L (left), giving BROTHEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive is a disreputable place, and a house of prostitution counts as a particularly low establishment of that kind.

clue.text: Animal the queen's extravagant over

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sitting over another means it comes first in the grid

blocks.note: OTT is short for over the top
ER is Elizabeth Regina; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A remark that the monarch is being lavish with spending.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter is a river-dwelling mammal of the weasel family, so it is a straightforward example of an animal.

clue.text: Producing movement of an involuntary kind by cattle

indicators.note: by means beside, so one piece is set next to the other

blocks.note: kine is an old plural of cow
a tic is a movement of the involuntary sort

explanation.surface: Seems to describe cows twitching without meaning to.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'movement' does double duty: it belongs to the definition, and the TIC is the involuntary kind of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinetic relates to motion and is used of energy or forces that cause things to move.

clue.text: Star turn embarrassed at taking a part, say

definitions.note: read as 'taking apart'; the answer is the plain verb

indicators.note: to turn the next word is to read it the other way round

explanation.surface: A leading performer blushes on being handed a role in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star turn' looks like one phrase meaning a headline act; it splits into the star and the instruction for the next word. 'Say' flags that 'a part' should be heard as 'apart'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sunder is to split or sever, which is what taking something apart does.

clue.text: Nude design for cover of book rejected as out of favour

indicators.note: a design rearranges the given letters into a new pattern
something rejected is sent back, so the word is read backwards
the rearranged letters form a cover placed around the other piece

blocks.note: VOL is the abbreviation for volume, a book

explanation.surface: A publisher turns down a naked cover picture as unsuitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unloved has lost the affection of others, which is to be out of favour with them.

clue.text: This may be out of order, so dieting is required

definitions.text: This may be out of order, so dieting is required

indicators.note: letters out of order are jumbled from their given sequence

explanation.surface: An upset stomach, so a diet is called for.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: when the gut is out of order, a diet is prescribed; and 'so dieting' put out of order gives the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Digestion is the bodily process that can go wrong, and a doctor may prescribe dieting when it does.

clue.text: Their contamination is no unusual consequence of a pest

definitions.text: Their contamination is no unusual consequence of a pest

indicators.note: unusual signals the preceding letters are put in an uncommon order

blocks.note: a rat is a classic pest

explanation.surface: Food supplies spoiled by vermin is a common occurrence.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue describes food allowances spoiled by rats; the pest supplies the first three letters and the mixed-up 'is no' the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Rations are fixed allowances of food, the stores a rat infestation would contaminate.

clue.text: The lady meets rising atmosphere of religious law

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word reads upwards, from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A woman encounters an increasingly devout mood.
explanation.walkthrough: SHERIA is a less common spelling of sharia.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharia is the body of Islamic law derived from the Koran and tradition, hence a religious law.

clue.text: Get nothing till a change takes place in London

indicators.note: a change means the preceding letters are altered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A grumble that you receive nothing until things alter.
explanation.walkthrough: Notting Hill Gate is a district and Underground station in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Notting Hill Gate is a named street and neighbourhood in west London, so it is a London place.

clue.text: Model finds artist in need of a drink

blocks.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: An artist's model discovers a painter who badly wants a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like an artist's sitter; it is the Model T Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirst is the sensation of wanting liquid, exactly the need for something to drink.

clue.text: Correction to original volume turns out louder

indicators.note: turning out here means the result is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: V is the symbol for volume

explanation.surface: An amended edition of a book is claimed to be noisier.
explanation.walkthrough: V goes inside NOISIER, between its second I and E, and the whole is then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A revision is an alteration that corrects or improves an earlier text, an emendation to the original.

clue.text: Lack of hair oil supplier, inter alia

indicators.note: to inter is to bury, so one piece is buried inside the other

blocks.note: OPEC is the cartel of oil-exporting countries

explanation.surface: Baldness listed among other things as a problem for an oil seller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inter alia' looks like the Latin phrase 'among other things'; it splits into a burying instruction and the word to bury in.
explanation.definitionFit: Alopecia is the medical term for hair loss, so it is a condition of lacking hair.

clue.text: Forecast gives poor signs of development

indicators.note: development turns the letters into something new by changing their order

explanation.surface: A gloomy outlook drawn from discouraging signs of growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A prognosis is a prediction, especially of how an illness will turn out, so it is a forecast.

clue.text: Stride out with the strongest 10

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone striding off who is the most parched of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 refers to the answer at 10-across, THIRST: the driest are the thirstiest.
explanation.definitionFit: The driest throat or person is the most parched, the one feeling the greatest craving for liquid.

clue.text: Fashionable way to make encroachment

explanation.surface: A trendy way of trespassing onto someone's ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An inroad is an advance into another's territory, an intrusion that gradually takes ground.

clue.text: Dotty uncle has a right to some kind of family

indicators.note: dotty means crazy, so the letters go haywire

explanation.surface: An eccentric uncle claims a place in a certain kind of family.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear family is the household unit of parents and children only, so nuclear names a kind of family.

clue.text: Stooped to get firing system in action

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: IGN is short for ignition, which fires an engine

explanation.surface: Bending down to make an engine's ignition work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stooped' means condescended here, not bent over.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to condescend to do something, and to stoop is to lower oneself in the same way.

clue.text: Dicky bathes in alcohol

indicators.note: dicky means unsound or faulty, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A man called Dicky soaks himself in drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name; it is British slang for unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green spirit flavoured with wormwood, so it is a kind of alcohol.

clue.text: Agree on condition of goods to be received

definitions.text: on condition of goods to be received

blocks.clueFragment: on condition of goods to be received
blocks.note: second meaning, split in two: goods arriving in the same state they were dispatched

explanation.surface: Signing up to delivery terms on how goods should arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning reads the answer as two words: goods received 'as sent'.
explanation.definitionFit: To assent is to give agreement; read as two words it describes delivery in dispatched condition.

clue.text: Hurried up to The House for a tutorial

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom

blocks.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, a British staple

explanation.surface: A student rushing to an Oxford college for a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The House' is the nickname of Christ Church, Oxford, which fits the tutorial; here it is just any house, a semi.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a small teaching session for discussion, much the same as a tutorial.

clue.text: Pet can be taken in the arms

indicators.note: taken in means fooled, so the letters are tricked into another order

explanation.surface: A small pet can be carried around cradled in your arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The hamster is a small rodent commonly kept by children as a household pet.

clue.text: Cast an eye over neckwear and smalls

blocks.note: to scan is to look over
ties are worn round the neck

explanation.surface: Glancing over someone's ties and underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Smalls is British slang for underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanties are skimpy women's knickers, and smalls is the British word for underclothes generally.

clue.text: What was famously "bust" in Miss West and Mrs French?

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the next

blocks.note: the Dambusters raid of 1943 burst German dams

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about which actress had a famous bust.
explanation.walkthrough: Mae West was famous for her figure, so 'bust' looks like a body joke; it points to the dams bust by the Dambusters.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is the French title for a married woman, the equivalent of the English Mrs.

clue.text: Ancient architectural style, or one in current use

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the following one

blocks.note: DC is direct current, a current in common use
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Asking whether an old building style is still employed today.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is the oldest and plainest of the classical Greek orders of columns and buildings.

clue.text: One's gran at a porn show could be unwelcome

indicators.note: what the letters could be shown as is a different arrangement of them

explanation.surface: A grandmother turning up at a blue movie would not be welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is Latin for an unacceptable person, used of expelled diplomats.
explanation.definitionFit: A persona non grata is someone not wanted or accepted, so the phrase describes being unwelcome.

clue.text: Perverted desire to live ...

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of its proper form, so the letters are twisted

explanation.surface: A twisted longing for life, trailing on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to live somewhere, having one's home or dwelling in that place.

clue.text: ... dealer said to be more perverted

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken, so its sound is what counts

blocks.note: grosser means more coarse or indecent

explanation.surface: Continues the previous clue: a trader reputed to be even more depraved.
explanation.definitionFit: A grocer is a shopkeeper who trades in food and household goods, so a kind of dealer.
